question_text: What distinguishes optimistic concurrency with Read-Copy-Update (RCU) from reader-writer locks (rwlock) in OS kernels?

options.text: Readers incur zero lock contention, zero atomic operations, and can execute concurrently with writers
Writers block readers until memory writes are completed
RCU requires exclusive hardware bus locks
RCU can only be used on single-core architectures

answer_explanation: RCU allows readers to traverse data structures without acquiring locks or executing atomic bus instructions. Writers create a copy, modify it, atomically swap pointers, and defer old memory reclamation.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: RCU allows readers to traverse data structures without acquiring locks or executing atomic bus instructions. Writers create a copy, modify it, atomically swap pointers, and defer old memory reclamation.
